system_description.narrative_title: U.S. economic offensive vs Iran and its ripple across energy and markets
system_description.narrative_summary: The single dominant narrative is the Trump administration's pivot to an intensified, US-led economic campaign ('economic D‑Day' led by Scott Bessent) to isolate and squeeze Iran, and the cascade of responses this triggers across oil markets, shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, regional diplomacy (notably Iran‑Oman talks), and reactions from major powers and trade partners. Treated as an open system, policy signals, sanctions and countermeasures exchange flows of capital, commodities, diplomatic leverage and information with external systems (global oil markets, China, regional states); feedback loops (oil‑price moves, secondary‑sanctions pressure on partners, domestic unrest in Iran, shipping disruptions) amplify or dampen further policy and market actions.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: US sanctions policy and announcement dynamics (Bessent/White House), Iran's economic and political response, Iran's regional diplomatic engagements (Oman, UAE, Iraq, Pakistan), major trade partners (China, India, etc.), global oil/trading flows and inventories, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, financial markets (oil prices, bonds, USD, Bitcoin), and immediate humanitarian/domestic effects in Iran (fuel queues, protests).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic and energy security system
adjacent_subsystems: Global crude oil and refined fuels market
International financial and sanctions architecture (secondary sanctions, trade finance)
Middle East regional security and diplomacy
Global shipping/logistics through strategic chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz)
evidence_headlines: Bessent’s sweeping sanctions against Iran send oil prices to their biggest drop in 3 weeks, while fueling hopes of de-escalation
Bessent Launches ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ to Isolate and Squeeze Iran
Oil drops 3% to 12-day low as Iran claims two-year plan to cope with Washington’s ‘economic D-Day’
Iran and Oman reach agreements on share of Hormuz and revenues, Revolutionary Guards say
China warns US it could retaliate over Iran sanctions
Iranians queue for petrol as US blockade bites

variables.name: Sanctions announcement intensity
variables.description: The frequency, scale and rhetorical force of official sanctions-related policy signals and public announcements.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strength
variables.description: The rigor and comprehensiveness of measures applied to restrict economic activity (scope of measures, targeting breadth and legal/operational tightness).

variables.name: Third‑party compliance with restrictions
variables.description: The degree to which external commercial and financial partners adhere to or circumvent imposed economic restrictions.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price for benchmark crude oil, reflecting supply–demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Shipping transit rate through chokepoints
variables.description: The rate of commercial vessel transits per unit time through strategic maritime chokepoints affecting trade flows.

variables.name: Shipping disruption rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of disruptive incidents to maritime traffic (attacks, seizures, detentions, mine threats) per unit time.

variables.name: Export volume from affected suppliers
variables.description: The volume of commodity exports originating from producers subject to economic pressure or sanctioning over time.

variables.name: Global oil inventory levels
variables.description: The aggregated stock of commercial and strategic crude and fuel inventories held across markets and storage facilities.

variables.name: Refinery capacity utilization
variables.description: The proportion of refining infrastructure throughput in operation relative to installed capacity, affecting refined product supply.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: The magnitude of short‑term price fluctuations across major financial asset classes (equities, bonds, FX, commodities, crypto).

variables.name: Capital outflow rate from targeted economy
variables.description: The rate at which financial capital leaves the economy under pressure (bank withdrawals, asset sales, cross‑border flows) per unit time.

variables.name: Secondary sanctions risk
variables.description: The perceived and actual probability that third parties will face punitive measures for maintaining economic links with the targeted economy.

variables.name: Regional diplomatic activity
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of diplomatic negotiations, mediations and channel engagements among neighboring actors over the issue.

variables.name: Domestic unrest intensity
variables.description: The level of civil disruption within the affected population, including protests, strikes, panic buying and political instability.

variables.name: Domestic fuel availability
variables.description: The accessibility and distribution adequacy of petrol and refined fuels to end users within the domestic market.

variables.name: Escalation expectations
variables.description: Market and policymaker expectations regarding the probability and scale of military or retaliatory escalation related to the economic campaign.

catalysts.title: Continued U.S. sanctions escalation
catalysts.description: Ongoing roll‑out of broad U.S. measures ('Operation Economic Outcast') and public threats to Iran partners, driving further sanctions announcements and enforcement steps.
catalysts.rationale: Bessent launches 'Operation Economic Outcast'; U.S. widens Iran sanctions; US threatens Iran’s economic partners.

catalysts.title: Iran‑Oman Hormuz corridor / demining talks
catalysts.description: Negotiations between Iran and Oman to create a temporary Strait of Hormuz corridor and mine‑clearing mechanism that could restore transit and calm markets.
catalysts.rationale: Iran and Oman eye temporary Hormuz deal; Oman foreign minister to visit Tehran; talks ongoing.

catalysts.title: Escalation of tanker strikes/mining in Hormuz
catalysts.description: Renewed tanker strikes, seizure threats and mine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz raise risks to shipping and energy markets.
catalysts.rationale: New tanker strike in Hormuz; Iran threatens 45–46 ships and vows retaliation for U.S. economic offensive.

catalysts.title: Return of U.S. diplomatic staff to Middle East missions
catalysts.description: Phased return of U.S. embassy personnel to the region, potentially lowering near‑term political tensions and market uncertainty.
catalysts.rationale: US prepares to send diplomats back; US starts returning staff to Middle East embassies.

catalysts.title: China pushes back against U.S. sanctions
catalysts.description: Beijing's warnings and threats of retaliation may blunt third‑party compliance and complicate U.S. enforcement choices.
catalysts.rationale: China warns it could retaliate; China vows to protect its rights as US readies Iran sanctions.

catalysts.title: Further U.S. SPR draws / low inventories
catalysts.description: Continued releases and low strategic stocks keep inventory levels tight, supporting a price premium for oil.
catalysts.rationale: Oil stocks in US SPR fall to lowest since 1982; U.S. crude inventories data mixed.

catalysts.title: Rising domestic unrest and panic buying in Iran
catalysts.description: Labor protests, panic buying and broader economic strain inside Iran are likely to intensify pressure on fuel availability and capital flight.
catalysts.rationale: Labor protests and panic buying signal growing pressure in Iran; Iranians queue for petrol.

catalysts.title: Third‑party firms avoid blacklisted Iran ships/trade
catalysts.description: Some oil companies and traders begin avoiding vessels and counterparties on U.S. blacklists, reducing Iranian export channels.
catalysts.rationale: Some oil companies to avoid ships on Iran blacklist; United States sanctions oil trader Wellbred over Iran links.
